the functional tuning of projection neurons in the antennal lobes of two closely related moth species, Heliothes subflexa and Heliothes virescens, is spatially conserved within the antennal lobs, but the functional tuning of the same neurons in the macroglomerural complex (MGC), a region of the antennal lops specialized for pheromones, is spatially divergent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how olfactory information is processed in insects.
the functional divergence of spatially and phylogenetically conserved olfactory structures.
the evolution of olfactory systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spatial map of glomeruli is conserved across individuals of the same species and between closely related species but that the functional map is not.
the MGC of H. subflexus and H. virescens is composed of a large cumulus and three satellite glomeruli, each of which is tuned to a different pheromone.
the functional tuning of olfactory glommeruli can be highly divergent, even when their spatial arrangement is conserved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial map of the MGC is invariant within a species but can vary between closely related species.
the spatial arrangement of the MGC in H. subflexus is invariant, and the functional tuning of the PNs that branch there is also invariant.

the spatial map within the MGC is invariant in the two species, and that the physiological tuning of the PNs is also invariant, but the association between the physiological tuning and spatial position of PNs has diverged.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the high degree of anatomical conservation, the functional organization of the macroglomerular complexes of these species has diverged.
, in these two closely related moth species, the same olfactory glomerular array is associated with different odorant tuning properties.

, although olfactory glomerular architecture is highly conserved across species, the functional organization of glomeruli can be altered in the context of species divergence, even when the spatial configuration of glomeruli remains unchanged.
